subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Multi-Variable Boundaries
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Multi-Variable Boundaries.

hook.text: A shipping form has weight (1–50 kg) and distance (1–1000 km). Each has boundaries. Together, they multiply.

buildup.text: When multiple inputs have ranges, boundary testing must consider each variable's edges independently.

discovery.text: Test each variable's boundaries while keeping others at nominal values. This isolates which variable fails.

twist.text: Interaction bugs hide at combined boundaries—max weight AND max distance together. Single-variable BVA misses these.

climax.text: Adding key combination boundary tests alongside single-variable tests catches the interaction defects.

punchline.text: One boundary at a time is good. Key combos are better.

quiz.question: What do multi-variable boundary tests catch?
